mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself jumped from -62.1 at t-1w to -50.3 at t-0w, an 11.8-point single-week gain after three weeks of stagnation near -60. This momentum reflects pent-up discretionary demand being released and is expected to persist, pulling the next-4-week mean above the last-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -62.1 to -50.3 week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC reverts to or below the -58 to -62 band for two consecutive weeks following t-0w, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility rose sharply from -56.3 at t-1w to -47.4 at t-0w (+8.9 points) after a prior dip, indicating renewed commuting activity. Once WORKPLACES week-on-week gains exceed 5 points, associated lunch and after-work errands lift RETAIL_REC within the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES increased from -56.3 to -47.4 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following a WORKPLACES jump greater than 5 points, the triggered mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in RESIDENTIAL (18.9 to 15.6) and rise in TRANSIT (-62.0 to -55.0) at t-0w jointly signal reduced stay-at-home behavior combined with restored transit usage, consistent with eased mobility restrictions. This joint shift is expected to drive higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks because both necessary conditions for discretionary outings (being away from home, having transport) improve together.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines while TRANSIT rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 18.9 to 15.6 while TRANSIT rose from -62.0 to -55.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite the joint RESIDENTIAL-down/TRANSIT-up pattern persisting, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility peaked at 46.0 at t-2w then declined to 22.3 at t-0w, consistent with a seasonal or weather-driven shift away from outdoor recreation. In a reopening regime, this redirected activity substitutes into indoor retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 46.0 at t-2w to 22.3 at t-0w
regime_hint: reopening phase with eased restrictions and seasonal transition
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a PARKS decline of this magnitude, the seasonal substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has oscillated near severe suppression, touching -62.0 at t-1w. If TRANSIT falls below -60 again, it signals renewed restriction or public caution around transit, which would choke off access to retail corridors and suppress RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -62.0 at t-1w before recovering to -55.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat in the two weeks after TRANSIT drops below -60, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained in a narrow band (-14.1 to -6.3) across all four weeks, indicating essential-trip demand is stable and decoupled from discretionary retail swings. Because essential mobility is not absorbing additional capacity, any slack in household mobility budgets flows into discretionary RETAIL_REC, supporting continued growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within an 8-point band across all four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM shows a sustained directional break (sudden rise or fall exceeding 10 points) and RETAIL_REC fails to follow the predicted direction, the decoupling hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS and RETAIL_REC show an inverse relationship this period: PARKS peaked at 46.0 at t-2w while RETAIL_REC simultaneously sat at a local low of -58.7, and as PARKS fell to 22.3 at t-0w, RETAIL_REC rose to -50.3. This substitution dynamic between outdoor and indoor activity is predicted to continue driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks as PARKS mobility further normalizes seasonally.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC rises
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 46.0 to 22.3 while RETAIL_REC rose from -58.7 to -50.3 over the same window
regime_hint: seasonal transition out of outdoor-recreation peak
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to decline but RETAIL_REC also declines over the next 28 days, the substitution interaction is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Despite the recent uptick, WORKPLACES mobility remains deeply suppressed, never exceeding -44.9 across all four weeks, consistent with an ongoing remote-work policy regime. This persistent ceiling on workplace activity caps commute-linked retail footfall, limiting how much RETAIL_REC can rise even as short-term rebounds occur, and is expected to pull the 4-week mean down relative to a scenario of full workplace recovery.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stayed between -44.9 and -56.3 across all four weeks
regime_hint: partial reopening with sustained remote-work mandates
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean rises substantially even while WORKPLACES remains below -44 throughout, the capped-recovery hypothesis is rejected.
